podcast.title: Audition for Zero (1999)
podcast.body: In March 1999, Chester was contacted by Jeff Blue to audition for Zero. He received two demo tapes—one with Mark Wakefield's original vocals and one instrumental—with the instruction to "Do your thing!" He wrote new lyrics, recorded his vocals, and sent them back, successfully passing the audition. "Chester wrote some new lyrics, recorded his vocals, and sent everything back. And that seal that he passed the audition."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Health Scare and Surgery (2003)
podcast.body: In May 2003, Chester was hospitalized for severe gastrointestinal issues, which were initially misdiagnosed as a viral infection or a complication from a spider bite received in 2001. The condition worsened dramatically during the filming of the "Numb" music video in Europe, leading to his return to the U.S. for surgery on a hiatal hernia, a condition causing extreme pain, heartburn, and vomiting, and potentially leading to esophageal cancer for someone who frequently screams. "He had to fly back to the States for surgery on a hiatal hernia, a condition that can lead to extreme pain, heartburn and lots of vomiting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Cyber-Stalking Incident (2006-2008)
podcast.body: Starting in 2006, Chester and his wife Talinda were subjected to a severe cyber-stalking campaign, which led to their cell phones, email, and PayPal accounts being compromised. The stalker, Devon Townsend, sent threatening messages, made silent calls, impersonated Chester's ex-wife, and repeatedly hacked their online accounts. The investigation, which involved a former Secret Service computer forensics expert, traced the activity to Sandia National Laboratories and eventually led to Townsend's arrest and conviction, resulting in a two-year jail sentence in February 2008 after her guilty plea in June 2007. "But the worst period was when he and Talinda were cyber-stocked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rock to Recovery Event (2016)
podcast.body: In October 2016, Chester attended "Rock to Recovery," an event focused on sober musicians. He greeted attendees at the door with his new puppy, appearing very happy and optimistic. "There's a story about Chester working an event called Rock to Recovery, which is all about sober musicians. This was in October 2016."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 2017 Europe Tour
podcast.body: In June and July 2017, Chester toured Europe with Linkin Park. Observers noted that he appeared to be in the best physical condition of his life during this period. "In June and July 2017, Lincoln Park toured Europe. The band was on fire. People remarked that Chester seemed to be in the best physical condition of his life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death (2017)
podcast.body: Chester Bennington died by suicide via hanging before 9 a.m. Pacific time on Thursday, July 20, 2017. This date also marked Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, with whom Bennington shared a very close bond. Cornell's death was "devastating" to Bennington, as both men battled drugs, alcohol, depression, and the pressures of being in a superstar band, ultimately described as "kindred spirits." "Chester Bennington died by his own hand, a hanging. One time before 9 a.m. Pacific time on Thursday, July 20th."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Suicide (2017)
podcast.body: Chester Bennington died on July 20, 2017, by hanging himself from a door in his bedroom, discovered by a housekeeper. The date of his death eerily coincided with what would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, suggesting a potential connection to Cornell's passing two months prior, which was described as breaking "something in Chester." Despite a vacation with his family in Arizona, Bennington returned to LA for an alleged Linkin Park video shoot, but "something went very wrong" that evening. No drugs or significant alcohol were found, and his autopsy revealed nothing of concern in his blood, leaving his motivations largely unknown. "The only possible clue is that July 20 would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Suicide (July 20, 2017)
podcast.body: Chester Bennington was found dead on July 20, 2017, around 9 AM, by his housekeeper at his home in Pollock's. He was alone, as his wife Talinda and children were away. The date tragically coincided with Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday. An empty bottle of vodka was found nearby, though nothing conclusive appeared in toxicology reports. "He was alone in the house the night of July 19, to Linda and the kids were away. Around nine in the morning of July 20, what would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, the family's housekeeper ran out to an arriving limo driver who was there to pick up Chester for a photo shoot. She'd found a body."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Suicide (July 20, 2017)
podcast.body: Chester Bennington, a good friend of Chris Cornell, died by suicide at his home in Los Angeles, two months after Cornell's death. This occurred on what would have been Chris Cornell's 53rd birthday, making it one of two particularly shocking suicides in 2017. "and then two months later on what would have been Chris's 53rd birthday, who's good friend Chester Bennington, at his home in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Death by Suicide (July 20, 2017)
podcast.body: On the morning of Thursday, July 20, 2017, at approximately 9 AM, a housekeeper found Chester Bennington hanging from a bedroom door at his house in Palos Verdes Estates. She alerted a driver who had arrived to pick him up for the TV commercial, and the driver subsequently called 911. "At around 9 a.m. on the morning of the 20th, a housekeeper found Chester hanging from a door in the bedroom."

podcast.title: Final Texts and Plans (July 2017)
podcast.body: In July 2017, while his wife Talinda and six children were on vacation in Arizona, Chester Bennington returned to Los Angeles on July 19, citing a television commercial shoot as the reason. Around the same time, he exchanged texts with Robert DeLeo of Stone Temple Pilots and Matt Sorum of Guns N' Roses, even floating the idea of performing with Sorum again in their band Kings of Chaos, with no alarm bells raised by anyone. "In July 2017, his wife, Talinda, and his family, he had six kids, went to Arizona on a vacation. But then on July 19th, he said he had to get back to LA."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Impact of Chris Cornell's Death (2017)
podcast.body: Chris Cornell's death in May 2017 deeply affected Chester Bennington, who attended Cornell's memorial service. Despite the difficulty, just days later, Bennington expressed feeling very creative, having written six new songs, and told friends, "we have to stick together, we have so much to live for." "But Chris Cornell's death really threw him for a loop. He attended Chris' memorial service, which was really hard."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Accident-Proneness and Tour Interruptions
podcast.body: Chester experienced a series of physical misfortunes, including breaking a wrist during a Melbourne show in 2007, falling ill while touring Asia in 2011 (causing five Linkin Park show cancellations), sustaining a shoulder injury requiring immediate surgery in 2011, and damaging his ankle playing basketball in 2015, which also necessitated surgery and further show cancellations. "he was rather accident prone. In 2007, he broke a wrist during a show in Melbourne. In 2011, he got sick while touring Asia, which affected five Lincoln Park shows. And then he injured his shoulder, which required immediate surgery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Acting Career
podcast.body: Chester pursued acting roles, including playing a stoner in a pharmacy in the 2006 movie "Crank" and a character in its sequel. He also had a minor role in the 2010 movie "Saw 3D" and played himself in the 2012 film "Art of Fact." "Acting, for example, he played a stoner and a pharmacy in the 2006 movie Crank."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Addiction and Depression Struggles
podcast.body: Chester experienced significant battles with drugs and alcohol, notably a crisis during his 2005 divorce. Although he married Talinda in 2006 and claimed to be "straight ever since," he contended with a persistent depression. In August 2016, he had a three-day bender involving alcohol and continued drinking until October 2016, and in June 2017, he confided to Ryan Schuck about an "hour by hour battle with addiction" following a relapse earlier that year where alcohol was the primary issue. "The drugs and alcohol were long behind them. Okay, there was that crisis in 2005 when he got divorced. But by marrying Tallinda in 2006, that was the best thing for him. He'd been straight ever since."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Addiction and Rehab History
podcast.body: Bennington went to rehab in 2006 and experienced a relapse in August 2016, which may have started as early as October 2015. There were also reports of a suicide attempt in November 2016, initially included in his 2017 autopsy report but later removed at his wife's request. "There was a trip to rehab in 2006, and something of a relapse in August 2016 that may have started as early as October 2015."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Audition for Zero
podcast.body: Chester was contacted by a VP of A&R at Zomba Music and asked to audition for a promising band in LA called Zero, which needed a frontman. He received two tapes from Zero—one with existing vocals by Mark Wakefield and another with instrumentals. He recorded his vocal interpretations over the instrumental tape and sent it back, successfully securing the position. "Chester was asked to provide some vocal interpretations for the music, record them over the instrumentals and then send the tape back."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Battle with Alcohol
podcast.body: Chester Bennington confided in Ryan Shuck, the guitarist from his side project Dead by Sunrise, about his "day-by-day battle with alcohol" through text messages, despite appearing to be in good spirits publicly. "He also spoke to Ryan Schuck, the guitarist in another one of his side projects called Dead by Sunrise. Schuck also had issues with alcohol. Some text messages went back and forth about what Chester described as his day-by-day battle with alcohol."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Contribution to Linkin Park's Name
podcast.body: Chester Bennington was credited with suggesting the name "Linkin Park" after driving past a real Lincoln Park in Santa Monica. The band also appreciated the national appeal of a name associated with Abraham Lincoln. "But it was Chester who came up with the name that stuck. He was driving past a real Lincoln Park in Santa Monica."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Creation of Dead by Sunrise
podcast.body: Chester initiated his side project, initially named Snow White Tan and later Dead by Sunrise, specifically to accommodate songs he had written that "weren't right for Lincoln Park," collaborating with friends from the bands Julian K and Orgy. "The group began because Chester had written some songs that really weren't right for Lincoln Park."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Creative Burst Post-Cornell Memorial
podcast.body: The day after Chris Cornell's memorial, Chester tweeted about feeling highly creative and having written six new songs. He also told a friend, "we have to stick together and we have so much to live for," indicating a sense of hope and a focus on survival. "The day after the memorial for Chris, Chester tweeted again, saying that he was feeling very creative and had written six brand new songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Date of Death and Cause
podcast.body: Chester Bennington, the vocalist for Linkin Park, was confirmed dead by his own hand on Thursday, July 20, 2017. His death came as a shock and was widely considered unexpected, even among a series of other musician deaths around that time. "Chester Bennington, vocalist with Lincoln Park, was not only dead, but dead by his own hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Dedicated Music Video Performance
podcast.body: Chester was renowned for never lip-syncing during the filming of music videos, always performing his vocals live and intensely for each take, even when suffering from severe gastrointestinal problems during the "Numb" video shoot. "Chester never lip-synced when filming music video. So he was going all out again and again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Defense of "One More Light" Sound
podcast.body: Facing fan criticism for the evolving sound of Linkin Park's "One More Light" album, Chester fiercely defended the band, pushing back against critics who accused them of "selling out" or "going soft." He expressed deep personal offense, later apologizing for his harsh words. "When you make it personal, like a personal attack who we are as people, like, dude, shut up. That means I can actually have feelings about it. And for most of my time, the feelings are, I want to kill you."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Devastation by Chris Cornell's Death
podcast.body: Chris Cornell's suicide on May 18, 2017, was a profound shock and devastating blow to Chester, who was already in an emotionally fragile state. Cornell was found dead in Detroit, just hours after a show. "The big shock was Chris Cornell's suicide. He was found dead early in the morning of May 18, 2017 in the MGM Grand Hotel in Detroit, just a couple of hours after the band played a show at the Fox Theatre the night before."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life Struggles
podcast.body: Chester Bennington came from a broken home and struggled with substance abuse early in his life, reportedly spending money earned at Burger King on "Coke and Crystal meth." His primary motivation during this difficult period was his dream of becoming a rock star. "He was from a broken home. He spent the money he made at Burger King on Coke and Crystal meth."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Life and Birthplace
podcast.body: Chester Bennington was born on March 20, 1976, in Phoenix. His mother was a nurse, and his father was a police detective whose work primarily focused on child sex abuse cases. "Chester was born on March 20th, 1976 in Phoenix."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Phoenix Bands
podcast.body: Before moving to Los Angeles to audition for Hybrid Theory (which became Linkin Park), Chester Bennington was active in the Phoenix music scene. Around age 17 in 1993, he sang in a band with his friend Sean, initially "Sean Dattel and his friends?" and then co-formed Gray Daze, which existed from late 1993 through 1998. "We now turn our attention to the parts that came together to form Lincoln Park, specifically what Chester Bennington was up to in Phoenix before he was invited to move to LA to sing for this new group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Relationships and Children
podcast.body: Chester's first partner was Elka Brandt, with whom he had a son named Jamie in 1996. After their separation, he married Samantha Olett and they had a son named Draven. "His first partner was a woman named Elka Brandt. They had a child in 1996 named Jamie. When they split, Chester married Samantha Olett and they had a child named Draven."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Warning Signs
podcast.body: Despite Linkin Park's outward success, there were subtle, slow-burning, almost undetectable internal struggles within Chester Bennington that, in hindsight, pointed to a tragic end six years later. "But if anyone had taken the time to really get to know Chester Bennington, there might have been some early warning signs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Family Life
podcast.body: At the time of his death, Chester Bennington had a loving family which included six children. "He had a loving family with six, six kids."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Final Interactions and Plans
podcast.body: On July 14, 2017, Chester filmed "Carpool Karaoke" looking great. On July 18, he spoke with longtime friend Sean Doudel of Gray Days, sounding great, and was later seen laughing and joking with his family in a video. On July 19, he emailed Matt Sorum about reforming the all-star covers band Kings of Chaos, expressing excitement. "On July 19, he sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer with guns and roses, saying that he would like to reform kings of chaos and all-star covers band. That'd be so much fun, he said."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Marriage and Divorce
podcast.body: Chester Bennington first married Samantha in 1996 at the age of 20. They had a son together before divorcing in 2005. "Mr. Bennington was married for the first time at age 20. This was back in 1996."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fragile Nature and Childhood Abuse
podcast.body: Chester Bennington possessed a certain fragility, openly discussing his childhood sexual abuse, struggles with addiction (including cocaine, meth, and alcohol), and depression. "Chester always had a certain fragility to him. He'd been sexually abused as a child, which he talked about."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Friendship with Chris Cornell
podcast.body: By the end of 2009, Chester Bennington and Chris Cornell had become "best friends," a close bond made tragic by their deaths within weeks of each other years later. "By the end of 2009, Chester had become good friends with Chris Cornell. Best friends, actually."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Friendship with Chris Cornell
podcast.body: Chester shared a close and long-standing friendship with Chris Cornell. They toured together, socialized frequently, and Chester was the godfather to Chris's son, Christopher. Their bond was evident in their joint performances and mutual support. "Chester and Chris had a friendship that went back years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Gray Daze Frustration
podcast.body: Despite Gray Daze being a local sensation in Phoenix, releasing two indie albums ("Wake Me" in 1994 and "No Sun Today" in 1997) and opening for international acts, they failed to attract major record labels. Burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, contemplating giving up music altogether, until he received the call to audition for Hybrid Theory. "So burned out and discouraged, Chester quit the group in 1998, and thought about giving up music called together."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: High School Bullying and Abuse
podcast.body: Chester's high school experience was difficult, marked by bullying and physical altercations. More profoundly, he was sexually abused by an older male friend from the age of seven until he was 13, an experience he kept secret due to shame and fear of not being believed. "High school was hell where he was bullied and beaten up. But that paled in comparison to the sexual abuse that was subjected upon him by an older male friend."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Identity Theft Incident
podcast.body: Chester and his wife Talinda experienced identity theft when a superfan from New Mexico managed to hack into Talinda's cell phone to steal their identities. "They live in Newport Beach, California, where they're still reeling from the time a superfan and New Mexico managed to steal their identities by hacking into Talinda's cell phone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Investigation Findings
podcast.body: No illicit drugs were found in the room, although a bottle of beer was present. The toxicology report indicated only trace amounts of alcohol in Bennington's blood, and while a prescription for a sleep aid was found, there were no significant concentrations in his bloodstream. The precise cause of his actions remains unknown. "No drugs were found, but a bottle of beer was found in the room. At the same time, the toxicology report noted that there was only a trace amount of alcohol and Chester's blood."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Later Marriage and Extended Family
podcast.body: Following the dissolution of his first marriage, Chester met and married Talinda Ann Bentley, a former Playboy model who became a schoolteacher, a relationship that endured for the remainder of his life. Together, they had three children—a boy and twin girls—expanding his family to include six children, alongside Jamie (from Elka Brandt), adopted Isaiah (Elka Brandt's other son), and Draven (from Samantha Olett). "He later met and married Talinda Ann Bentley, who was a former playboy model, turned schoolteacher, and that relationship held together for the rest of Chester's life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Marriage and Career Frustration
podcast.body: By 1998, a young Chester Bennington was married, despite both he and his wife being barely 20. Feeling completely frustrated with his lack of progress in the music industry, he quit his band Grey Daze and took a job as an assistant with a digital services company. "But by then, he was completely frustrated with his lack of progress in the music biz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Music as an Escape
podcast.body: Music provided a crucial escape for Chester Bennington during his difficult teenage years, becoming a significant and positive outlet. "Fortunately, music became a bigger and better escape."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Influences
podcast.body: Bennington cited Scott Weiland of Stone Temple Pilots and Dave Gahan of Depeche Mode as his musical heroes, though the transcript notes these were "not exactly guys whose lifestyle should be emulated." "Although his heroes were Scott Wyland of the Stone Temple Pilots and Dave Gahn of Depeche Mode, not exactly guys whose lifestyle should be emulated."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musician's Expressiveness
podcast.body: Chester Bennington's ability to articulate deep feelings and concepts through his music resonated with millions of fans, significantly contributing to Linkin Park's sales success. "many on the strength of Chester's abilities to express how he felt, feelings that resonated with so many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: North American Tour & Gray Days Reunion Plans
podcast.body: Following the Europe tour, a short break was planned before a 29-date North American tour in support of the number one album "One More Light." Around this time, Chester was also discussing a potential reunion with Gray Days, his pre-Linkin Park band from Arizona. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Openness about Mental Health
podcast.body: Chester was remarkably candid about his struggles with mental health and depression, describing his internal world as a "bad neighborhood" he shouldn't navigate alone. He expressed that actively engaging in his roles as a father, husband, bandmate, and friend helped him cope with the challenges of life on life's terms. "He talked about depression, substance abuse, being sexually molested as a kid. His thinking was that if he could talk about it, well, maybe that would encourage others to do the same thing, maybe get some help."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Openness about Mental Health
podcast.body: Chester was remarkably honest about his struggles with mental health and actively encouraged others to speak out and seek help. This transparency was a significant aspect of his public persona and legacy. "Chester was really, really good about being honest about his mental health. He encouraged many, many people to take that first step to talk about things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Parents' Divorce and Custody
podcast.body: When Chester was 11 years old, his parents divorced, and his father was granted custody. This event significantly impacted him, leading him to delve deeply into drug use. "Mom and dad divorced when Chester was 11, dad got custody."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Personal Life Prior to Death
podcast.body: Chester had a very close relationship with his wife, Talinda, and his family, who meant everything to him. They had recently purchased a new house in a beautiful, gated community. Before the planned Linkin Park tour, he and Talinda enjoyed a two-week vacation, and he exchanged happy, positive texts with members of Stone Temple Pilots, expressing optimism for the future. "Chester and his wife and his family were super tight. They meant everything to him."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Personal Struggles and Fragile Nature
podcast.body: Chester Bennington battled significant personal issues throughout his life, including childhood abuse, addiction to cocaine and methamphetamine, a drinking problem, persistent depression, multiple failed attempts at rehabilitation, and previous suicide attempts. He was described as having a "certain fragile nature," finding solace in his friendship with Chris Cornell, with whom he often shared his struggles. "He had all sorts of issues, abused as a child, addiction to coke and meth, a drinking problem, lingering depression, failed attempts at rehab, a couple of suicide attempts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Proactive Approach to Mental Health
podcast.body: Bennington was actively involved with "Rock to Recovery," an organization comprised of sober musicians dedicated to helping others struggling with addiction. "Chester had been proactive about his condition. He was a member of an organization called Rock to Recovery, which consisted of sober musicians, looking to help those who weren't."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Restrictions and Early Job
podcast.body: After moving in with his mother at 17 due to his drug use, Chester was essentially permanently grounded, with his only approved outings being for his shifts at Burger King. "he was basically permanently grounded, except for his shifts in Burger King."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Second Marriage and Family
podcast.body: Following his divorce from Samantha, Chester married former Playboy model Talinda Bentley. They had a son named Tyler and resided in Newport Beach, California. "he since married a former playboy model named Talinda Bentley. They have a son named Tyler."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Struggles with Addiction and Depression
podcast.body: Despite public perceptions, Chester relapsed in 2006, requiring a trip to rehab for drug and alcohol problems. He also battled depression, a condition not always externally visible, but one he openly discussed alongside substance abuse and childhood sexual molestation, hoping to inspire others to seek help. "The truth was that he had relapsed in 2006, requiring a trip to rehab. He was also suffering from depression, a condition that's not always apparent to people on the outside."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Teenage Drug Abuse
podcast.body: As a teenager, Chester Bennington experimented with a wide range of drugs, including pot, coke, various opioids, LSD, and meth. His father, a police officer, was unable to manage his drug abuse, leading Chester to move in with his mother at the age of 17. "As a teenager, he tried everything. Pot, Coke, various opioids, LSD, meth, basically the whole buffet."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tragic Death
podcast.body: A few months after giving a radio interview in early 2017 where he openly discussed his mental health battles, Chester Bennington died by suicide. "A few months after that interview, Chester would be gone, taking his own life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tribute Performance at Cornell's Funeral
podcast.body: At Chris Cornell's funeral, Chester performed Leonard Cohen's "Hallelujah." He later tweeted about Cornell's voice, describing it as encapsulating joy, pain, anger, forgiveness, love, and heartache, and helping him understand these complexities within himself. "At the funeral, Chester sang Leonard Cohen's hallelujah, and he wrote this on his Twitter, your voice was joy and pain, anger and forgiveness, love and heartache all wrapped up into one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Upcoming Tour and Reunion Plans
podcast.body: At the time of his death, Chester Bennington was preparing for a 29-date Linkin Park tour and had committed to a reunion with his former band, Grey Daze, after the tour concluded. He appeared happy, secure, and in excellent physical condition. "A 29-date Lincoln Park tour was about to start, and once that was over, he'd committed to joining Gray Days, the band he was in before Lincoln Park, for a reunion."

xref.title: Identity Theft by Nuclear Lab Technologist – Devon Townsend, Albuquerque, 2006
xref.body: In late winter 2006, Chester Bennington's wife Talinda began receiving threatening calls and texts, friends were called from the hacked number, and Talinda lost access to her eBay and PayPal accounts. Chester hired a former Secret Service specialist who traced the intrusion to a 27-year-old single mother named Devon Townsend, employed as a technologist at a nuclear weapons research facility in New Mexico. Townsend had initially found Chester's email address in a mass email accidentally sent out to promote a tattoo parlor Chester co-owned in Tempe, Arizona. She used his birthday and zip code to access his .Mac account, then guessed his password as "Charlie" (his middle name), gaining access to email addresses, photos, home addresses, social security numbers, and bank account details — though she did not steal any money. She was arrested and charged with multiple offenses. "She was a fan. And she was bored at her job."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Performance with Chester Bennington (2008)
xref.body: During the 2008 Project Revolution Tour, Chris Cornell was performing when Chester Bennington unexpectedly joined him on stage to sing "Hunger Strike." This Temple of the Dog song was written by Cornell as a tribute to his late roommate, Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont. "If we go back to the 2008 project revolution tour, Chris was on the bill. And when he stepped forward to sing the Temple of Dog Song, Hunger Strike, a song written for and dedicated to Chris's late roommate Andrew Wood of Mother Lovevont, Chester surprised everybody by coming in to sing with him."

xref.title: Chester Bennington Joins (2013)
xref.body: In May 2013, after firing Scott Weiland, the band announced that Chester Bennington of Linkin Park would join as a full-time member. This arrangement lasted about 18 months, during which they toured extensively and released one 5-track EP. "In May of that year, they announced that Chester Bennington of Lincoln Park was the new guy and as a full-time member too."

xref.body: Despite Chester Bennington's suicide in 2017, Stone Temple Pilots remained determined to continue. They held a very long series of auditions, which began in February 2016 and concluded on November 14, 2017. "They ran from February 2016 and didn't end until November 14th, 2017."

xref.body: On July 14, 2017, the band filmed an episode of "Carpool Karaoke" with James Corden. Footage from the event showed Chester Bennington appearing happy and healthy just days before his death. "On July 14, 2017, the band shot an episode of Carpool Karaoke with James Corden. That seemed to be loads of fun."

xref.title: Chester Bennington Tribute Concert (2017)
xref.body: On October 27, 2017, a three-hour tribute concert for Chester Bennington was held at the Hollywood Bowl. The event featured friends from Blink 182, System of a Down, Korn, and Avenged Sevenfold, and was streamed live, reaching millions of viewers as Linkin Park paid tribute to their fallen bandmate. "On October 27th, 2017, there was a three hour tribute to Chester featuring his friends from Blink 182, system of a downed corn, a bench, seven fold and more."

xref.title: Chester Bennington's Suicide (2017)
xref.body: Chester Bennington committed suicide on July 20, 2017, after returning to Linkin Park from his temporary role in Stone Temple Pilots. "But then we all know what happened next, Chester committed suicide on July 20th of 2017."

xref.title: Chester's Addiction Battle (2017)
xref.body: In June 2017, Chester Bennington confided in his friend Ryan Schuck about his struggles related to this side project, revealing that he was enduring "an hour by hour battle with addiction" just months before his death. "But in June 2017, he did tell his friend Ryan Schuck of his side project, Dead by Sunrise, and he was suffering, and this is a quote, an hour by hour battle with addiction."

xref.title: Death by Suicide (May 18, 2017)
xref.body: Chris Cornell died by suicide by hanging on May 18, 2017, at 1:30 AM, a death that came as a "real shock" to many. He was found in his hotel room (room 1136 at the MGM Grand, Detroit) with a red exercise band around his neck, attached to a carabiner jammed tightly into the doorframe. The night before, May 17, Soundgarden played a show at the Fox Theatre in Detroit, after which his long-time tour manager felt Chris was "messed up and struggling." Back at the hotel, his bodyguard, Martin Kirsten, gave him two Ativan pills, for which Chris had a prescription. Shortly after, Chris spoke to his wife Vicki, who noted his slurred speech; he claimed to have taken "too much Ativan" and was "just tired." He abruptly hung up, alarming Vicki. Martin Kirsten, called by Vicki, found Chris's room latched from the inside. After kicking open both the room and bathroom doors, he found Chris. The toxicology report found Ativan (four doses), pseudoephedrine, butylbital, caffeine, and Narcan (administered by paramedics). While his wife speculated drugs contributed to an "altered mental state," the police ruled it suicide by hanging. "Chris was pronounced dead at 1.30, and the police ruled a suicide by hanging."

xref.title: Proposed Reformation (2017)
xref.body: On July 19, 2017, Chester Bennington sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer of Guns N' Roses, expressing his enthusiasm for reforming Kings of Chaos, which he described as an "all-star covers band." This communication occurred less than 24 hours before Chester's death. "On July 19, he sent an email to Matt Sorum, the former drummer with guns and roses, saying that he would like to reform kings of chaos and all-star covers band. That'd be so much fun, he said."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reunion Discussions (2017)
xref.body: In the summer of 2017, Chester Bennington was actively discussing a reunion with Gray Days. On July 18, 2017, he spoke with Sean Doudel, a band member he had known since they were teenagers, who reported that Chester "sounded great" during their conversation. "Chester was talking about a reunion with Gray Days, a band from his pre-Lincoln Park days in Arizona."

xref.title: Return with Lineup Changes (2024)
xref.body: After a long hiatus following Chester Bennington's death, Linkin Park reportedly returned to the music scene in late 2024, featuring a couple of lineup changes. This marked the band's official re-emergence after a period of adjusting to the loss of their former frontman. "It was only in late 2024 that they returned with a couple of lineup changes."

xref.title: Close Friendship with Chester Bennington
xref.body: Chris Cornell was a very close friend of Chester Bennington, and his death significantly impacted Bennington. "We can't talk about the death of Chris Cornell, without immediately going to Chester Bennington of Lincoln Park. He and Chris were great, great friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Close Relationship with Chester Bennington
xref.body: Chris Cornell and Chester Bennington were described as "very, very close" and "kindred spirits." Cornell's death, which occurred on what would have been his 53rd birthday (the same day Bennington died), was "devastating" to Bennington. Both men battled drugs, alcohol, depression, and the pressures associated with being in a superstar band. "Chester and Chris were very, very close, and Chris's death was devastating to Chester."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Creative Break and Side Projects
xref.body: After the intense touring cycle for Meteora, the band collectively requested and took downtime. This period allowed members to rest and "pursue some other projects" (like Chester Bennington's Dead by Sunrise and the Jay-Z collaboration "Collision Course") to revitalize their creative energies. "Besides, it would be good to rest and then maybe pursue some other projects to restore the creative juices."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death Date Coincidence – 37 Years After Ian Curtis, Close to Chester Bennington
xref.body: Cornell died by hanging on May 18, 2017 — exactly 37 years to the day that Joy Division singer Ian Curtis hanged himself. Two months later, on July 20, 2017 (which would have been Cornell's 53rd birthday), his close friend Chester Bennington of Linkin Park died by suicide, also by hanging. Cornell is interred at Hollywood Forever Cemetery in Los Angeles; his tombstone reads "Voice of our generation and an artist for all time." Johnny Ramone's monument is nearby. "Two months after Chris died, July 20, 2017, which would have been Chris' 53rd birthday, his close friend Chester Bennington of Linkin Park died by suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extended Hiatus After Chester Bennington's Death
xref.body: Following the death of lead singer Chester Bennington in July 2017, Linkin Park entered a prolonged period of inactivity as the remaining members grappled with the loss and adjusted to the tragedy. The band was absent from the music scene for a considerable time, with their eventual return in late 2024 accompanied by lineup changes. "Lincoln Park was absent from the scene for a long, long time after Chester's death as everybody tried to adjust."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Friendship with Chester Bennington
xref.body: Chris Cornell maintained a close friendship with Linkin Park's Chester Bennington, with both artists frequently commiserating about their shared personal demons and struggles. This bond was tragically underscored by Bennington's death by suicide a couple of months after Cornell's, on what would have been Cornell's 53rd birthday. "Chester and Chris were great, great friends, often commiserating about their various personal demons."

xref.title: Influence on Side Project Name
xref.body: Chester Bennington's initial name for his side project, "Snow White Tan," was noted as a potential reference to David Bowie and his iconic Ziggy Stardust persona. "Notice the reference to Bowie and Zee Stardust."

xref.title: Inspiration for "One Step Closer" Lyrics
xref.body: Chester Bennington directly addressed Don Gilmore through the lyrics of "One Step Closer," expressing frustration over Gilmore's "blind dismissal" of his lyrical submissions and the pressure he exerted. The "shut up" part in the song was 100% directed at Gilmore. "Chester is actually talking to producer Don Gilmore with these words about how he so blindly dismissed Chester whenever he submitted lyrics for his inspection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: LP Recharge Online Game
xref.body: Chester Bennington was involved in the creation of "LP Recharge," an online action game based on the band itself. The game was launched through Facebook, demonstrating the band's engagement with new digital platforms. "He was also involved in the creation of LP Recharge, which was an online action game based on the band and launched through Facebook."

xref.title: Name Change from Hybrid Theory
xref.body: The band changed its name to "Linkin Park" from "Hybrid Theory" after being inspired by an actual park of the same name in Santa Monica that they drove by daily. They believed it to be a universally recognizable name, as many American towns reportedly have a Lincoln Park. "Hybrid Theory became the deliberately misspelled Lincoln Park."

xref.title: One More Light Fund Establishment
xref.body: In memory of Chester Bennington, Linkin Park established the "One More Light Fund," an organization dedicated to offering help and support to individuals grappling with mental health issues. xref.title: Origin as Snow White Tan
xref.body: Chester Bennington's side project was initially known as "Snow White Tan," a name that was recognized as a possible reference to David Bowie and his Ziggy Stardust persona, before eventually changing to Dead by Sunrise. "his own side project, which was first called Snow White Tan. Notice the reference to Bowie and Zee Stardust, and then Dead by Sunrise."

xref.title: Producer of Hybrid Theory
xref.body: Don Gilmore produced Linkin Park's debut album, Hybrid Theory. His demanding approach in the studio caused significant tension with the band, particularly with Chester Bennington. "He was driving them nuts with the way he was pushing them in the studio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Record Deal with Warner Brothers
xref.body: Linkin Park signed with Warner Brothers Records in late 1999, a deal facilitated by an A&R executive named Jeff who had previously recommended Chester Bennington to the band (then Zero) and later became a VP at Warner Brothers. This signing occurred despite Warner Brothers having rejected the band three times previously. "they got a meeting, and they were signed in late 1999."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Three Singers Post-Weiland – Chester Bennington Moonlighted from Linkin Park; Jeff Gutt Won Online Audition
xref.body: Scott Weiland was fired and rehired multiple times; the first replacement attempt involved David Coutts in a short-lived side project called Talk Show that failed entirely. Weiland was fired for good in 2013; he died of a drug overdose in 2016 without reconciling with the band. Chester Bennington of Linkin Park — a lifelong STP fan — was brought in for approximately two and a half years, was made an official member, toured, and recorded two tracks before returning to Linkin Park. His replacement was Jeff Gutt, found through an online audition that also briefly considered John Borja from the Philippines; Gutt had been a runner-up on Season 3 of *The X Factor* and was confirmed by fall 2017. "Chester was also a lifelong STP fan since, well, since he could remember."
